Each one\\u0027s handoff follows, in\\ndispatch order \\u2014 the run that opened the work first, its follow-ups after it.\\n\\n[Run 1 of 4 \\u00B7 1a257a68]\\n\\n- **What exists:** The feedback step end to end: the project setting (team field) and task override, the hold at the three release doors plus queueing, \\u0060FeedbackStepEngine\\u0060 and its loop, the \\u0060FeedbackCheck\\u0060 model role, the check and judging prompts, a feedback-step mode in the plan engine, and the \\u0060task show\\u0060, \\u0060status\\u0060, \\u0060task queue\\u0060 and \\u0060task next\\u0060 surfaces.\\n- **Gotchas:**\\n  - The hold decision is resolved by the caller that can see the project and recorded on the event: \\u0060TaskAssignCommand\\u0060, \\u0060TaskDependencyResolver\\u0060 and \\u0060RemoteStackedParentSweep\\u0060 each do it. A new Blocked-to-Queued door has to pass \\u0060FeedbackStepRules.Holds\\u0060 too.\\n  - A note recorded on another node needs the fleet to pass the trust rule. Engine tests stamp notes with the beginning node for that reason.\\n  - Engine tests share one Postgres database per class, so each test abandons the tasks it seeded.\\n- **Left undone on purpose:**\\n  - No second step when a parent changes after the child starts.\\n  - No goal run.\\n  - The check does not read the blockers\\u0027 pull request summaries.\\n  - No plan-wide default for the flag.\\n  - The unplaced-task race and held-task takeover noted above.\\n\\n[Run 2 of 4 \\u00B7 ea58d997]\\n\\n- What now exists: the revise fence for feedback overrides. \\u0060FeedbackStepRules.RefuseClaimWhenQueueingWouldHold\\u0060, which \\u0060h9k task start\\u0060 and \\u0060h9k task drive\\u0060 call. \\u0060Frontmatter.Keys\\u0060, and an allowlist-based \\u0060FeedbackRevisionRules\\u0060. Both projections now mirror the aggregate\\u0027s per-blocker removal.\\n- Gotcha: a task in a project with the step on and every blocker finished cannot be started or driven straight from Published. Queue it so the step runs, or turn the step off for that task with \\u0060h9k task revise --feedback-step off\\u0060. A start that still waits on a blocker, with the acknowledgement flag, is unaffected.\\n- Left undone on purpose, as three ideas: the one-shot ledger marker for cross-node replication lag, binding the holder release to the exact acquisition, and fencing the release sweeps\\u0027 appends. Each changes the ledger format or touches pre-existing dispatcher or sweep paths, so it does not belong in this diff.\\n\\n[Run 3 of 4 \\u00B7 de7ad6f3]\\n\\n- Nothing new was written this lap. The branch already held all four review fixes, folded into their owning commits on top of current \\u0060origin/main\\u0060. This lap re-checked them with a build and the touched test classes, then recorded the four fix replies for the platform to post after it pushes.\\n- The remote head is still the old \\u00605519866ce\\u0060, so the push will be a force-with-lease replacing pre-rebase history. That is expected. The reply text describes the fixes; it does not cite commits.\\n- The full \\u0060dotnet test\\u0060 gate was not run here. It belongs to the daemon\\u0027s serialized host gate.\\n\\n[Run 4 of 4 \\u00B7 9be7e04f]\\n\\n- **What now exists:** the \\u0060PlanParkReason.RevisionBeyondText\\u0060 description is the new generic sentence, \\u0060docs/cli.md\\u0060 lists \\u0022reassigned\\u0022 as an ended-without-acting cause, and \\u0060FeedbackStepCommandTests\\u0060 has a DB-free test of the Published-parked \\u0022Feedback outcome\\u0022 row. All three are folded into their owning commits, with tree identity verified.\\n- **Gotcha:** a feedback step\\u0027s parked outcome reason is the \\u0060PlanParkReason\\u0060 description (\\u0060FeedbackStepEngine.ParkText\\u0060). Changing that text breaks substring assertions in \\u0060FeedbackStepEngineTests\\u0060, which is why one assertion moved with it.
